sentences.text: Lee Whitfield (client) disclosed he lost his job in January at the depot.
Lee Whitfield stated the Universal Credit housing element went wrong, causing rent to build up.
Lee Whitfield disclosed arrears of £3,850, estimated to be for three or four months.
Lee Whitfield disclosed he received court papers for a hearing on 9 December at Harbridge County Court.
Lee Whitfield disclosed the claim is a possession claim on rent arrears grounds (ground eight, ten, and eleven) by Ashcroft Lettings.
Lee Whitfield disclosed he has lived in the flat for six years.
Lee Whitfield disclosed he lives alone with a cat.
Lee Whitfield disclosed he offered £50 a month in September, but the landlord rejected it, stating they wanted it all.
Lee Whitfield disclosed the landlord's rejection of the payment plan was in a text message on his phone.
Lee Whitfield disclosed there is damp in the bedroom, described as 'black up the wall', and stated he has told the landlord and has photos.
Lee Whitfield disclosed he has other debts: Council tax (bailiffs letter), a credit card debt of about £2,000, and electricity on a meter.
Lee Whitfield disclosed he has no help with debts and has stopped opening mail.
Lee Whitfield disclosed he went to his GP in March after taking an overdose of 16 paracetamol, which his neighbour found and resulted in an ambulance call and an overnight stay.
Lee Whitfield disclosed he received no follow-up from the GP after the March incident, other than a nurse calling a couple of times.
Lee Whitfield disclosed he has not hurt himself since March.
Lee Whitfield disclosed he thought about ending his life this week (Sunday night) but did not do anything.
Lee Whitfield disclosed he is currently safe and feeling a bit better after talking about the situation.
Lee Whitfield disclosed he put the housing cost problem on his Universal Credit journal twice with no answer.
Lee Whitfield disclosed he has the tenancy agreement, rent statement, Universal Credit statements since January, and damp photos.
Lee Whitfield disclosed he can email the remaining documents by Friday 27th.
Lee Whitfield disclosed his priority is to avoid losing the flat.
Lee Whitfield disclosed he wants to resolve the Universal Credit issue.
Lee Whitfield disclosed he wants to resolve the other debts.
Sophie Grant advised she would file a defence and counterclaim regarding the damp.
Sophie Grant advised she would ask the court to adjourn the hearing if more time is needed to sort Universal Credit.
Sophie Grant advised she would refer Lee to the Citizens Advice debt team to apply for a breathing space (60 days).
Sophie Grant advised she would write to Universal Credit regarding the housing costs.
Sophie Grant advised she would provide the crisis team number and Samaritans (116 123).
Sophie Grant advised she would ring Lee's GP today.
Sophie Grant advised they would ring the GP together.
